title: Big Pharma Can Rival Big Software | Andreessen Horowitz
gist: a16z argues pharma already matches software in scale (Eli Lilly >$1T, ~300 $1B+ drugs vs ~190 software companies in the same revenue range) and that AI, by raising probability of success and cutting time to approval, could break Eroom's law and earn pharma companies software-like 'platform valuation credit' for their discovery engines. It maps the emerging AI-pharma stack (data/lab automation, predictive biology, reasoning agents, molecular design, model harnesses, full-stack biotechs) while flagging that biology remains data-poor, complex and non-verifiable in silico.

insights.claim: The top 30 pharma companies represent roughly $5T of market cap, and 9 public pharma companies are worth over $200B versus 16 software companies in the same size bracket.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Large-cap pharma is a comparable-scale sector to large-cap software; relative-value framing between the two is legitimate.

insights.claim: Eli Lilly's GLP-1 portfolio generated close to $17B in Q3 2026, nearly matching Anthropic's revenue in that quarter, and analysts expect it to exceed $100B in annual sales by 2030.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: A single drug class at Lilly is on the scale of a frontier AI lab's revenue; GLP-1 trajectory is the key driver of Lilly's $1T+ valuation.
insights.quote: In Q3 2026 alone, Lilly’s GLP-1 portfolio did close to $17B, nearly matching Anthropic’s revenue in that quarter.
insights.locator: Eli Lilly alone has a market

insights.claim: Eli Lilly's injectable GLP-1 portfolio (Mounjaro and Zepbound) did nearly $40B in 2025 sales, roughly matching Salesforce's revenue over the same period.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Top drug franchises are equivalent in revenue to mega-cap software companies yet trade at very different multiples.

insights.claim: About 300 drugs (29% of branded drugs on the market) are projected to generate $1-10B in peak annual sales, compared with roughly 190 public software companies with revenue in the same range.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: There are more billion-dollar drug 'businesses' than billion-dollar-revenue public software companies.

insights.claim: The three largest therapeutic categories by sales are oncology (30% of global drug sales), metabolic disorders including GLP-1s (18%), and immunology (11%); biologics account for 42% and small molecules 43% of global pharmaceutical revenue.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Market-size map for where AI drug discovery value is likely to accrue.

insights.claim: Pharma has a dual economic structure: drug development is a power-law hits business, while an approved, patent-protected drug becomes an annuity business.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: AI that improves hit rates attacks the risky half while leaving the annuity half intact, which compounds returns.
insights.quote: It is a hits business in drug development and an annuity business once a drug succeeds and is approved.
insights.locator: There is a duality to pharma

insights.claim: Drug revenues follow a near power-law distribution: the top 25% of drugs generate about 85% of revenues, and for the top 10 pharma companies about 50% of revenues come from their top 3 assets.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Pharma equity risk is concentrated in a few assets; single-asset events dominate valuations.

insights.claim: Revenue concentration is extreme at leaders: 63% of Eli Lilly's 2025 revenue came from its GLP portfolio and 54% of Merck's 2025 revenue came from Keytruda alone.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Merck faces large patent-cliff exposure on Keytruda; Lilly is highly levered to GLP-1 durability.

insights.claim: A typical drug enjoys 10-14 years of exclusivity after launch and reaches peak sales about 6 years post-launch, but standouts like Dupixent (launched 2017, ~$18B in 2025 sales, U.S. patent expiry expected 2031) grow for over a decade via serial indication expansion.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Indication expansion is the lever that turns drugs into long-duration growth assets; watch 2031 for Dupixent LOE.

insights.claim: Both first-in-class and best-in-class strategies can produce dominant drugs: Keytruda was first-in-class in U.S. PD-1, while Skyrizi won despite being third to market in IL-23, and both exceeded $30B in peak sales.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Being late to a validated mechanism is not disqualifying; AI-improved best-in-class molecules are a viable investment thesis.
insights.locator: There are large winners in both

insights.claim: Patent cliffs force pharma to continually replace revenue, as when AbbVie's Humira revenue fell from $20B in 2022 to $4B in 2025 after loss of exclusivity, which drives big pharma's acquisitive behavior.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Loss-of-exclusivity cliffs are the structural engine of pharma M&A demand for biotech assets.
insights.locator: Pharma companies typically don’t get much

insights.claim: U.S. prescription drug spending has more than doubled over the past decade, yet the FDA still approves only about 40-50 novel drugs per year, and roughly two-thirds of big pharma's new drugs are sourced via acquisitions or licensing.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Big pharma is an external buyer of innovation, creating exit demand for biotechs that discover drugs more efficiently.
insights.locator: 2. HOW AI COULD CHANGE DRUG ECONOMICS

insights.claim: Amortizing failures, the present-value cost of developing a drug is close to $2B and takes 13 years on average, with fewer than 5% of drug candidates reaching FDA approval and fewer than 10% of drugs entering human trials being approved.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Baseline for measuring whether AI drug companies are actually bending cost and success curves.

insights.claim: AI could reduce the present-value cost of a drug in two ways, raising probability of success and shortening time to approval, which could make previously uneconomical targets viable and make AI-native therapeutics companies structurally more profitable.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Track clinical success rates and cycle times of AI-native biotechs as the key proof points for higher R&D ROIC.
insights.locator: AI could reduce the present-value cost

insights.claim: AI is expected to usher in an era of drug candidate abundance, with time and cost savings across target selection, in silico molecule prioritization, trial protocol design, patient recruitment and FDA document drafting, though some steps like chronic toxicology studies remain regulation-bound.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Candidate abundance shifts the bottleneck to validation and clinical capacity rather than discovery.
insights.locator: As the team at Formation Bio

insights.claim: The global CRO market is $90B ($30B discovery/preclinical, $60B clinical), and wet-lab demand is expected to explode as AI accelerates candidate generation and AI labs seek more training data, benefiting data providers and robotic lab automation companies.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Second-order beneficiaries of AI drug discovery are wet-lab capacity, CROs and lab-automation vendors (picks and shovels).
insights.quote: We expect wet lab demand to explode as generating drug candidates becomes faster, and AI labs seek more data on which to train their models.
insights.locator: Moving a drug through the pipeline

insights.claim: Large pharma is valued mainly by DCF on approved and post-Phase 2 drugs, typically at 8-20x P/E or 3-7x revenue with 20-40% net margins, giving little credit to the drug discovery engine itself.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Early pipelines are a rounding error in pharma valuations, a potential mispricing if discovery becomes repeatable.

insights.claim: If AI makes drug discovery repeatable, investors may start valuing pharma companies' discovery engines like software platforms, rewarding predictable replacement of patent-cliff revenue with software-like multiples.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Potential multiple re-rating for pharma companies that demonstrably industrialize AI discovery; watch for analysts crediting platforms.
insights.quote: If drug discovery becomes more repeatable, investors may begin to more directly value the strength of a pharma company’s discovery engine
insights.locator: If drug discovery becomes more repeatable

insights.claim: Biotechs have historically been forced to deprioritize platform investment because investors assign value to individual assets; AI-driven capital efficiency and 'platform valuation credit' could lower biotech cost of capital and enable broader pipelines.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: a16z and Eli Lilly launched The Biotech Ecosystem Fund to back this thesis; platform biotechs may command premiums.
insights.locator: Recognizing the value of technology platforms

themes.theme: Why now: Bio x AI at GPT-3 moment

insights.claim: a16z believes Eroom's law, the decades-long decline in drug R&D productivity, has finally met an equal and opposite force in continuous frontier model improvement.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Core bull thesis; rising approvals per R&D dollar would be the confirming signal.
insights.quote: We believe Eroom’s law has finally found its equal and opposite force: continuous frontier model improvement.

insights.claim: Bio x AI is near GPT-3-level market maturity, with biological models starting to generalize across many tasks with little task-specific training, and scaling laws appear to hold in molecular generation as models train on larger experimental datasets.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Implies a multi-year capability ramp over the next 5 years; proprietary experimental data becomes the scaling input.
insights.quote: We think we are close to the GPT-3 level of market maturity in Bio x AI today
insights.locator: We think we are close to

insights.claim: Two model vectors drive progress: LLM/reasoning models automating scientist knowledge work (literature review, experiment design, analysis, regulatory filing) and diffusion-based structure models enabling de novo molecule generation and optimization.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Distinguishes productivity-tool plays from molecule-design plays when evaluating bio-AI companies.

insights.claim: Big pharma is signing many AI partnerships: Isomorphic Labs has deals with J&J, Novartis and Eli Lilly (up to $1.2B and $1.7B in milestones with Novartis and Lilly), and Chai Discovery, Boltz, BigHat Bio, Nabla Bio, Genesis Molecular AI and Profluent each partner with multiple pharmas.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Commercial validation exists, but the next test is whether model gains translate into better drugs entering the clinic.
insights.locator: Beyond model releases, there are signs

insights.claim: Frontier AI labs are moving into drug discovery: Anthropic opened a wet lab and announced its own drug candidates for neglected diseases, and OpenAI acquired Orchestra Bio to build an agentic layer for biotech program execution.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Frontier labs could become competitors to bio-AI startups and even drug developers; their long-run role is still in flux.

insights.claim: Bio-AI startups can either sell data and technology to pharma and frontier labs or develop drugs themselves; the latter takes more risk and capital but offers more upside, and some pursue both.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Business-model choice determines capital intensity and return profile for bio-AI investments.
insights.locator: 4. THE NEW BIO BUSINESSES AI COULD UNLOCK

insights.claim: Veeva, a vertical software company with about a $50B market cap and $100M+ contracts with its largest accounts, is a precedent that large businesses can be built selling technology to pharma.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Veeva is the comp for the ceiling of tools-to-pharma businesses; such precedents are few.

insights.claim: The technology-seller layer comprises five categories: data providers and lab automation (Medra, Tacit, Latch, BigHat Bio), predictive models of biology (Axiom Bio, insitro, Noetik, Radical Numerics, Inductive Bio), scientific reasoning agents (Edison Scientific, Phylo), molecular design (Chai, Boltz), and model harnesses/enterprise deployment (Valkai, Collate).
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Market map of the AI-pharma stack for sourcing and competitive analysis.
insights.locator: Within this approach, we’re seeing several

insights.claim: High-quality data is described as a huge bottleneck for the AI drug industry, making robotic lab automation, expert data collection and benchmarking a key opportunity.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Proprietary experimental data is the moat; data-generation businesses may capture durable value.
insights.quote: High-quality data is a huge bottleneck for this industry.

insights.claim: a16z is most excited about vertically integrated, full-stack AI therapeutics companies such as Recursion, Isomorphic, insitro, Xaira, Relay Tx and Octant Bio, which capture full value from internal assets and run a closed loop between lab data, models and clinical results.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Public proxies like Recursion are bellwethers for whether the full-stack AI biotech model works.

insights.claim: Biology lacks an internet-scale training corpus: the Protein Data Bank, the largest high-fidelity public protein dataset, holds only about 300K experimentally determined 3D structures amassed over 50 years.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Data scarcity caps model progress and raises the value of proprietary experimental data generation.

insights.claim: Better molecular design will not necessarily yield more effective drugs without understanding which biological mechanisms to target, a point argued by insitro founder Daphne Koller.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Target biology, not molecule design, may be the binding constraint; be skeptical of design-only plays.
insights.locator: Biology is a highly complex system

insights.claim: Unlike math or coding, drug designs cannot yet be fully validated in silico; validation requires wet labs and long, regulated human clinical trials, so how much AI can speed biopharma feedback loops remains unknown.
insights.speaker: Caroline Goggins, Justin Kahl, Alex Immerman, Michael Cialone, Paxton Paine, Vineeta Agarwala
insights.so_what: Payoffs from AI drug discovery will lag model progress by years; expect long timelines before clinical proof.
